rows.label: Screens affected

questions.q: Is the stated age floor eighteen, or thirteen with a consent path built before the law requires it?
questions.lede: The DPDP Rules' consent section comes into force 14 May 2027, eighteen months after the Act's commencement notice.

items.label: Plan states no age; default set to 18

visual.note: Eighteen months from the commencement notice's own publication date.
visual.caption: A real date for the consent duty; the plan's answer need not wait for it.

questions.stakes: Choosing thirteen now means building a verifiable-consent path on a schedule the law sets, not one the studio picks.
state: DPDP section 9 requires verifiable parental consent for anyone under eighteen.
Gazette CG-DL-E-14112025-267647, G.S.R. 843(E): section 9 comes into force eighteen months after 14 November 2025, so 14 May 2027.
The plan states no age floor today.
tension: The pilot itself runs and ends before the section is even in force.
Thirteen widens the reachable audience today, at the cost of a consent path that has to exist by the same date.

options.label: Eighteen, stated in the terms and the sign-in fine print
gains: No consent path to build before the pilot.
options.screens: S01 fine print states the floor.

options.label: Thirteen, with a consent path built before 14 May 2027
gains: A wider reachable audience from day one.
costs: A verifiable-consent flow, confirmed by counsel, has to ship before that date.
options.screens: Sign-in gains an age check and a consent step.

recCase: The pilot ends before section 9 is even in force, so nothing forces this yet.
Eighteen needs zero new engineering before the first stranger signs in.
questions.flip: A pilot cohort skewing markedly younger than expected would argue for building the consent path early instead of waiting.
sources: Gazette CG-DL-E-14112025-267647 and CG-DL-E-14112025-267650, read 17 September 2026

questions.q: Do the audit's stop and continue lines hold for the twenty-person pilot, or do the founders set their own?
questions.lede: An earlier revision's pilot section listed measures with no thresholds at all.

rows.label: Kit recipients who run the kickoff
Name the problem unprompted
cells: One person asks how to pay

visual.caption: The same twenty-person pilot, read for a reason to stop or continue.

questions.stakes: A pilot with no numbers attached to it cannot fail, and a plan that cannot fail is not being tested.
state: An earlier revision listed pilot measures with no thresholds.
The audit's design sizes both lines to the same twenty-person pilot and ten kit recipients.
tension: Any threshold the founders pick is at least as defensible as the audit's; the only failure is picking none.
Setting the bar too low makes a weak pilot look like a pass.

options.label: Adopt the audit's stop and continue lines
gains: A number exists before the pilot starts, not after.
costs: Not the founders' own judgement call.

options.label: Set different numbers
gains: Reflects the founders' own risk appetite.
costs: Needs deciding before the pilot, not during it.

recCase: The lines are sized to the pilot the plan already describes.
Adopting a number now is strictly better than the section that had none.
questions.flip: A founder judging four of twenty active as too easy a bar would justify tightening it before the pilot starts.
